title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 114: The Secrets of the Peat Bog Bodies
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 114 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Secrets of the Peat Bog Bodies

Paragraph 1. Across wet peat bogs in northern Europe, workers and scientists have found hundreds of ancient human bodies. Many of these 'bog bodies' are over two thousand years old. Unlike dry mummies from hot deserts, bog bodies still keep their soft skin, hair, and fingernails. Because their faces look almost alive, they help scientists learn about life and death in ancient times.

Paragraph 2. Special bog water protects the bodies from rotting. Wet peat bogs are full of a soft green plant called moss. Over thousands of years, dead moss sinks down and creates still water with no oxygen inside. Normal bacteria cannot live without air, so they cannot eat the bodies. Also, the moss makes the water very sour and acidic. This acid turns human skin into dark brown leather. However, the strong acid often melts away the hard bones inside the body.

Paragraph 3. The most famous bog body is Tollund Man, found in Denmark in 1950 by people cutting peat for fuel. He lay on his side wearing a warm sheepskin hat. His face looked so clear that local police first thought someone had killed him only a few days earlier. Later, experts saw a rope around his neck and studied his stomach. His last meal was a thick grain porridge made with wild seeds, with no meat at all.

Paragraph 4. Two hundred years ago, historians thought bog bodies were bad criminals punished by law. Today, archaeologists often find valuable bronze weapons, gold rings, and fine pots buried near the bodies. Because people left rich gifts beside them, experts now believe many bog bodies were killed during ancient religious ceremonies to ask gods for good harvests.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...creates still water with no oxygen inside."
Đoạn 2: "This acid turns human skin into dark brown leather."
Đoạn 3: "...local police first thought someone had killed him only a few days earlier."
Đoạn 3: "His last meal was a thick grain porridge made with wild seeds..."

q5.text: Peat bog bodies lose all of their skin and fingernails quickly after burial.

steps: Đoạn 1: Xác ướp đầm lầy vẫn giữ được da mềm, tóc và móng tay (keep their soft skin, hair, and fingernails).

q6.text: Acid in the bog water can cause human bones to break down and disappear.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...the strong acid often melts away the hard bones inside the body."

q7.text: University students discovered Tollund Man during a planned science dig in 1950.

steps: Đoạn 3: Người tìm ra là những người đi cắt than bùn làm chất đốt (people cutting peat for fuel), không phải sinh viên đại học.

q8.text: Tollund Man ate a large meal of cooked meat just before he died.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bữa ăn cuối chỉ có cháo ngũ cốc và hạt dại, hoàn toàn không có thịt (with no meat at all).
